german: Könnten wir bitte die Speisekarte haben?
english: Could we please have the menu?
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for die Speisekarte.
situation: When ordering or requesting die Speisekarte (the menu) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for the menu.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Könnten wir bitte die Speisekarte haben?
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: Could we please have the menu?

german: Bringen Sie uns bitte die Weinkarte.
english: Please bring us the wine list.
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for die Weinkarte.
situation: When ordering or requesting die Weinkarte (the wine list) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for the wine list.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Bringen Sie uns bitte die Weinkarte.
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: Please bring us the wine list.

german: Haben Sie eine aktuelle Tageskarte?
english: Do you have a current specials menu?
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for die Tageskarte.
situation: When ordering or requesting die Tageskarte (the daily specials menu) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for the daily specials menu.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Haben Sie eine aktuelle Tageskarte?
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: Do you have a current specials menu?

german: Bringen Sie mir bitte die Rechnung.
english: Please bring me the bill.
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for die Rechnung.
situation: When ordering or requesting die Rechnung (the bill) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for the bill.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Bringen Sie mir bitte die Rechnung.
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: Please bring me the bill.

german: Das Trinkgeld ist schon mit eingerechnet.
english: The tip is already factored in.
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for das Trinkgeld.
situation: When ordering or requesting das Trinkgeld (the tip) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for the tip.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Das Trinkgeld ist schon mit eingerechnet.
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: The tip is already factored in.

german: Ich trinke ein großes Helles.
english: I will drink a large lager beer.
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for ein helles Bier.
situation: When ordering or requesting ein helles Bier (a light lager beer) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for a light lager beer.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Ich trinke ein großes Helles.
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: I will drink a large lager beer.

german: Ein kaltes Hefeweizen, bitte.
english: A cold wheat beer, please.
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for ein Weißbier / Weizen.
situation: When ordering or requesting ein Weißbier / Weizen (a wheat beer) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for a wheat beer.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Ein kaltes Hefeweizen, bitte.
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: A cold wheat beer, please.

german: Eine große Apfelschorle, bitte.
english: A large apple juice spritzer, please.
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for eine Apfelschorle.
situation: When ordering or requesting eine Apfelschorle (apple spritzer) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for apple spritzer.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Eine große Apfelschorle, bitte.
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: A large apple juice spritzer, please.

german: Ein Glas stilles Wasser für mich.
english: A glass of still water for me.
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for ein stilles Wasser.
situation: When ordering or requesting ein stilles Wasser (still water) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for still water.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Ein Glas stilles Wasser für mich.
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: A glass of still water for me.

german: Ich nehme eine Tasse Kaffee mit Milch.
english: I'll take a cup of coffee with milk.
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for eine Tasse Kaffee.
situation: When ordering or requesting eine Tasse Kaffee (a cup of coffee) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for a cup of coffee.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Ich nehme eine Tasse Kaffee mit Milch.
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: I'll take a cup of coffee with milk.

german: Welchen Kuchen haben Sie heute?
english: Which cakes do you have today?
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for ein Stück Kuchen.
situation: When ordering or requesting ein Stück Kuchen (a piece of cake) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for a piece of cake.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Welchen Kuchen haben Sie heute?
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: Which cakes do you have today?

german: Als Vorspeise nehme ich die Suppe.
english: As an appetizer I'll take the soup.
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for die Vorspeise.
situation: When ordering or requesting die Vorspeise (the appetizer) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for the appetizer.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Als Vorspeise nehme ich die Suppe.
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: As an appetizer I'll take the soup.

german: Als Hauptgericht nehme ich den Lachs.
english: For the main course I'll take the salmon.
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for das Hauptgericht.
situation: When ordering or requesting das Hauptgericht (the main course) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for the main course.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Als Hauptgericht nehme ich den Lachs.
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: For the main course I'll take the salmon.

german: Möchten Sie noch eine Nachspeise?
english: Would you like a dessert?
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for die Nachspeise / das Dessert.
situation: When ordering or requesting die Nachspeise / das Dessert (the dessert) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for the dessert.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Möchten Sie noch eine Nachspeise?
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: Would you like a dessert?

german: Was ist die heutige Tagessuppe?
english: What is today's soup of the day?
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for die Tagessuppe.
situation: When ordering or requesting die Tagessuppe (the soup of the day) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for the soup of the day.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Was ist die heutige Tagessuppe?
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: What is today's soup of the day?

german: Gibt es auch etwas Vegetarisches?
english: Is there also something vegetarian?
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for ein vegetarisches Gericht.
situation: When ordering or requesting ein vegetarisches Gericht (a vegetarian dish) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for a vegetarian dish.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Gibt es auch etwas Vegetarisches?
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: Is there also something vegetarian?

german: Kann ich Pommes als Beilage haben?
english: Can I have fries as a side dish?
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for die Beilage.
situation: When ordering or requesting die Beilage (the side dish) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for the side dish.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Kann ich Pommes als Beilage haben?
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: Can I have fries as a side dish?

german: Könnten wir einen leeren Teller zum Teilen bekommen?
english: Could we get an empty plate to share?
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for ein zusätzlicher Teller.
situation: When ordering or requesting ein zusätzlicher Teller (an extra plate) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for an extra plate.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Könnten wir einen leeren Teller zum Teilen bekommen?
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: Could we get an empty plate to share?

german: Mir fehlt leider noch eine Gabel.
english: Unfortunately I am still missing a fork.
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for ein Besteck.
situation: When ordering or requesting ein Besteck (cutlery / silverware) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for cutlery / silverware.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Mir fehlt leider noch eine Gabel.
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: Unfortunately I am still missing a fork.

german: Könnten Sie mir noch eine Serviette bringen?
english: Could you bring me another napkin?
literalTranslation: Word breakdown for eine Serviette.
situation: When ordering or requesting eine Serviette (a napkin) in a restaurant or café.
culturalNote: Standard polite dining phrasing in German-speaking countries when asking for a napkin.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen sonst noch etwas bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Könnten Sie mir noch eine Serviette bringen?
dialogue.englishA: Can I bring you anything else?
dialogue.englishB: Could you bring me another napkin?

german: Der Rest ist für Sie.
english: Keep the change.
literalTranslation: The rest is for you.
situation: When paying your bill at a restaurant, café, or in a taxi to tip the server/driver.
culturalNote: In Germany, tipping (Trinkgeld) is typically given directly when handing cash or stating the rounded total to the server, rather than leaving money on the table.

dialogue.speakerA: Das macht dann 18 Euro 50, bitte.
dialogue.speakerB: Hier sind 20 Euro. Der Rest ist für Sie!
dialogue.englishA: That comes to 18.50 euros, please.
dialogue.englishB: Here is 20 euros. Keep the change!

german: Stimmt so!
english: Keep the change! / That's fine!
literalTranslation: It is correct like this!
situation: Said when handing over cash and telling the waiter or cashier not to give you change.
culturalNote: The most common short phrase for rounding up the bill at bars, bakeries, and casual diners in Germany and Austria.

dialogue.speakerA: Zwei Cappuccino, das macht 7 Euro 80.
dialogue.speakerB: Hier sind 10 Euro. Stimmt so!
dialogue.englishA: Two cappuccinos, that's 7.80 euros.
dialogue.englishB: Here is 10 euros. Keep the change!

german: Zusammen oder getrennt?
english: Together or separately?
literalTranslation: Together or separated?
situation: Asked by German waitstaff when bringing the bill to determine if guests want split bills.
culturalNote: Splitting the bill (getrennt zahlen) item by item is standard and completely acceptable in Germany; servers carry mobile bill pouches to calculate each person's share.

dialogue.speakerA: Wir möchten bitte bezahlen.
dialogue.speakerB: Gerne. Zusammen oder getrennt?
dialogue.englishA: We would like to pay, please.
dialogue.englishB: Certainly. Together or separately?

german: Wir möchten getrennt zahlen, bitte.
english: We would like to pay separately, please.
literalTranslation: We would like to pay separated, please.
situation: Telling the server that each person in the group will pay for their own food and drinks.
culturalNote: The server will go around the table and ask each person what they ordered.

dialogue.speakerA: Möchten Sie zahlen?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, wir möchten bitte getrennt zahlen.
dialogue.englishA: Would you like to pay?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, we would like to pay separately, please.

relatedPhrases: Ich zahle mein Schnitzel und das Bier.

german: Könnten wir bitte zahlen?
english: Could we please pay? / Check, please!
literalTranslation: Could we please pay?
situation: Politely catching the waiter's attention to request the final bill.
culturalNote: In Germany, waitstaff rarely bring the check automatically until you specifically request it, so you can sit and chat undisturbed.

dialogue.speakerA: Entschuldigung, könnten wir bitte zahlen?
dialogue.speakerB: Sehr gerne, ich komme sofort zu Ihnen.
dialogue.englishA: Excuse me, could we please pay?
dialogue.englishB: Very gladly, I will be right with you.

german: Die Rechnung, bitte.
english: The check, please.
literalTranslation: The bill, please.
situation: Direct and polite way to request the restaurant bill.
culturalNote: Commonly accompanied by making eye contact and raising an index finger slightly.

dialogue.speakerA: Haben Sie noch einen Wunsch?
dialogue.speakerB: Nein danke, die Rechnung bitte.
dialogue.englishA: Do you have any other wish?
dialogue.englishB: No thank you, the check please.

german: Das geht auf mich!
english: This is on me! / My treat!
literalTranslation: That goes onto me!
situation: Offering to pay the entire bill for a friend or group.
culturalNote: Used among friends, dates, or colleagues when celebrating or inviting someone.

dialogue.speakerA: Wer bezahlt die Pizza?
dialogue.speakerB: Lass mal, das geht heute auf mich!
dialogue.englishA: Who is paying for the pizza?
dialogue.englishB: Don't worry, this is on me today!

german: Ich lade dich ein.
english: I'm inviting you. / My treat.
literalTranslation: I invite you.
situation: Explicitly stating you will pay for the meal or drink.
culturalNote: In German culture, inviting someone ('Ich lade dich ein') firmly implies that you will cover their expenses.

dialogue.speakerA: Kommst du mit zum Mittagessen?
dialogue.speakerB: Ich habe wenig Geld dabei. - Kein Problem, ich lade dich ein!
dialogue.englishA: Are you coming along for lunch?
dialogue.englishB: I have little money with me. - No problem, my treat!

german: Haben Sie einen Tisch für zwei Personen?
english: Do you have a table for two people?
literalTranslation: Have you a table for two persons?
situation: Arriving at a restaurant without a reservation and asking for seating.
culturalNote: At busier German restaurants, reserving in advance ('einen Tisch reservieren') is strongly recommended.

dialogue.speakerA: Guten Abend! Haben Sie einen Tisch für zwei Personen?
dialogue.speakerB: Guten Abend! Ja, hier drüben am Fenster.
dialogue.englishA: Good evening! Do you have a table for two people?
dialogue.englishB: Good evening! Yes, over here by the window.

german: Ich habe einen Tisch auf den Namen Weber reserviert.
english: I reserved a table under the name Weber.
literalTranslation: I have a table on the name Weber reserved.
situation: Checking in with the restaurant host upon arrival.
culturalNote: German reservations are always referenced by last name.

dialogue.speakerA: Guten Abend, willkommen!
dialogue.speakerB: Hallo, ich habe einen Tisch auf den Namen Weber reserviert.
dialogue.englishA: Good evening, welcome!
dialogue.englishB: Hello, I have reserved a table under the name Weber.

german: Ist hier noch frei?
english: Is this seat/table free?
literalTranslation: Is here still free?
situation: Asking to sit at an unoccupied seat at a shared table in a brewery, café, or train.
culturalNote: Sharing large wooden tables with strangers is normal in German beer gardens (Biergärten) and traditional pubs (Kneipen). Always ask before sitting down.

dialogue.speakerA: Entschuldigung, ist hier noch frei?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja klar, bitte nehmen Sie Platz!
dialogue.englishA: Excuse me, is this seat free?
dialogue.englishB: Yes of course, please have a seat!

german: Ich hätte gerne...
english: I would like to have...
literalTranslation: I would have gladly...
situation: The polite, universal formula for ordering food, drinks, or goods.
culturalNote: Much more polite and natural than saying 'Ich will' (I want).

dialogue.speakerA: Was darf ich Ihnen bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Ich hätte gerne ein Schnitzel mit Bratkartoffeln.
dialogue.englishA: What may I bring you?
dialogue.englishB: I would like a schnitzel with fried potatoes, please.

german: Ich nehme das Gleiche.
english: I'll have the same.
literalTranslation: I take the same.
situation: Ordering identical food or drink as your dining partner.
culturalNote: Quick and natural way to order when following someone's recommendation.

dialogue.speakerA: Für mich ein Helles Bier, bitte.
dialogue.speakerB: Und für mich bitte das Gleiche!
dialogue.englishA: For me a light beer, please.
dialogue.englishB: And for me the same, please!

german: Was können Sie empfehlen?
english: What can you recommend?
literalTranslation: What can you recommend?
situation: Asking the server for recommendations or house specialties.
culturalNote: Waitstaff in Germany are usually very honest about what is fresh or local.

dialogue.speakerA: Ich kann mich nicht entscheiden. Was können Sie empfehlen?
dialogue.speakerB: Unser Sauerbraten mit Klößen ist heute hervorragend.
dialogue.englishA: I can't decide. What can you recommend?
dialogue.englishB: Our Sauerbraten with dumplings is excellent today.

relatedPhrases: Was ist die Spezialität des Hauses?

german: Was ist die Spezialität des Hauses?
english: What is the house specialty?
literalTranslation: What is the specialty of the house?
situation: Inquiring about the dish the restaurant is most proud of.
culturalNote: Great for discovering regional culinary traditions in different German states.

dialogue.speakerA: Was ist denn die Spezialität des Hauses?
dialogue.speakerB: Probieren Sie unsere frische Forelle Müllerin Art.
dialogue.englishA: What is the specialty of the house?
dialogue.englishB: Try our fresh trout meunière style.

german: Haben Sie auch vegetarische oder vegane Gerichte?
english: Do you also have vegetarian or vegan dishes?
literalTranslation: Have you also vegetarian or vegan dishes?
situation: Inquiring about plant-based options on the menu.
culturalNote: Most German restaurants clearly label vegan (V) and vegetarian (VG) options nowadays.

dialogue.speakerA: Haben Sie auch vegetarische Gerichte?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, alle Gerichte mit dem grünen Blatt sind vegetarisch.
dialogue.englishA: Do you also have vegetarian dishes?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, all dishes with the green leaf are vegetarian.

german: Ist dieses Gericht laktosefrei?
english: Is this dish lactose-free?
literalTranslation: Is this dish lactose-free?
situation: Asking about allergens or dairy content.
culturalNote: German dining establishments are legally required to provide an allergy menu (Allergenkarte).

dialogue.speakerA: Ich vertrage keine Milch. Ist die Suppe laktosefrei?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, die Suppe wird mit Kokosmilch zubereitet.
dialogue.englishA: I cannot tolerate milk. Is the soup lactose-free?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, the soup is prepared with coconut milk.

german: Könnten wir noch etwas Brot haben?
english: Could we have some more bread?
literalTranslation: Could we still some bread have?
situation: Requesting an extra basket of bread for the table.
culturalNote: In some German eateries bread is complimentary, while in others a small basket fee applies.

dialogue.speakerA: Entschuldigung, könnten wir noch etwas Brot haben?
dialogue.speakerB: Selbstverständlich, ich bringe Ihnen sofort frisches Brot.
dialogue.englishA: Excuse me, could we have some more bread?
dialogue.englishB: Of course, I'll bring you fresh bread right away.

relatedPhrases: Könnten wir noch eine Portion haben?
Bringen Sie uns bitte noch Wasser.

german: Ein Glas Leitungswasser, bitte.
english: A glass of tap water, please.
literalTranslation: A glass pipe-water, please.
situation: Ordering tap water instead of bottled mineral water.
culturalNote: In Germany, when you order 'Wasser' you are almost always given sparkling bottled mineral water (Mineralwasser mit Kohlensäure). You must explicitly ask for 'Leitungswasser' or 'Stilles Wasser'.

dialogue.speakerA: Möchten Sie etwas trinken?
dialogue.speakerB: Ein Glas Leitungswasser, bitte.
dialogue.englishA: Would you like something to drink?
dialogue.englishB: A glass of tap water, please.

german: Ein stilles Wasser, bitte.
english: A still (non-carbonated) water, please.
literalTranslation: A quiet water, please.
situation: Ordering bottled water without carbonation.
culturalNote: Default German mineral water has gas (mit Kohlensäure / Sprudel). Saying 'stilles Wasser' ensures no bubbles.

dialogue.speakerA: Welches Wasser möchten Sie?
dialogue.speakerB: Ein großes stilles Wasser, bitte.
dialogue.englishA: Which water would you like?
dialogue.englishB: A large still water, please.

german: Guten Appetit!
english: Enjoy your meal! / Bon appétit!
literalTranslation: Good appetite!
situation: Said to companions before starting to eat.
culturalNote: It is polite etiquette in Germany to wait until everyone is served and someone says 'Guten Appetit' before taking the first bite.

dialogue.speakerA: Das Essen ist da!
dialogue.speakerB: Guten Appetit! - Danke, gleichfalls!
dialogue.englishA: The food is here!
dialogue.englishB: Enjoy your meal! - Thanks, same to you!

german: Lass es dir schmecken!
english: Enjoy your food! (informal)
literalTranslation: Let it taste to you!
situation: Friendly wish to a close friend or family member as they eat.
culturalNote: Casual equivalent of 'Guten Appetit'.

dialogue.speakerA: Hier ist dein Teller.
dialogue.speakerB: Danke, lass es dir auch schmecken!
dialogue.englishA: Here is your plate.
dialogue.englishB: Thanks, enjoy yours as well!

german: Zum Wohl! / Prost!
english: Cheers! / To your health!
literalTranslation: To well-being! / Cheers!
situation: Toast when drinking wine (Zum Wohl) or beer (Prost).
culturalNote: Essential German toast etiquette: always look each person directly in the eyes when clinking glasses, or legend says you get 7 years of bad luck!

dialogue.speakerA: Auf unseren Urlaub!
dialogue.speakerB: Prost! In die Augen schauen!
dialogue.englishA: To our vacation!
dialogue.englishB: Cheers! Look into the eyes!

german: Hat es Ihnen geschmeckt?
english: Did you enjoy your meal?
literalTranslation: Has it tasted to you?
situation: Asked by the waiter when clearing plates.
culturalNote: A polite inquiry. The standard affirmative answer is 'Ja, es war ausgezeichnet!'

dialogue.speakerA: Darf ich die Teller mitnehmen? Hat es Ihnen geschmeckt?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, vielen Dank, es war wirklich köstlich!
dialogue.englishA: May I take the plates? Did you enjoy your meal?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, thank you very much, it was really delicious!

german: Es war ausgezeichnet, vielen Dank!
english: It was excellent, thank you very much!
literalTranslation: It was excellent, many thanks!
situation: Complimenting the meal to the waitstaff or cook.
culturalNote: Expressing genuine appreciation for a well-prepared meal.

dialogue.speakerA: Wie war das Steak?
dialogue.speakerB: Es war ausgezeichnet, vielen Dank!
dialogue.englishA: How was the steak?
dialogue.englishB: It was excellent, thank you very much!

relatedPhrases: Ein großes Lob an die Küche.

german: Ein großes Lob an die Küche!
english: Compliments to the chef/kitchen!
literalTranslation: A big praise to the kitchen!
situation: Sending special praise back to the kitchen staff.
culturalNote: Used when a meal significantly exceeded your expectations.

dialogue.speakerA: War alles zu Ihrer Zufriedenheit?
dialogue.speakerB: Absolut, ein großes Lob an die Küche!
dialogue.englishA: Was everything to your satisfaction?
dialogue.englishB: Absolutely, compliments to the kitchen!

german: Könnten wir das bitte einpacken lassen?
english: Could we please get this wrapped to go? / Doggy bag, please.
literalTranslation: Could we that please pack let?
situation: Asking to take leftover food home.
culturalNote: Taking leftovers home ('zum Mitnehmen einpacken') is very common in Germany today.

dialogue.speakerA: Ich schaffe die Portion nicht mehr. Könnten wir das bitte einpacken lassen?
dialogue.speakerB: Sehr gerne, ich bringe Ihnen eine Box.
dialogue.englishA: I can't finish this portion. Could we please get this packed to go?
dialogue.englishB: Certainly, I'll bring you a container.

german: Kann ich hier mit Karte zahlen?
english: Can I pay by card here?
literalTranslation: Can I here with card pay?
situation: Asking if credit or debit card is accepted.
culturalNote: While card payment is increasingly accepted, some traditional German venues and kiosks still prefer or require cash ('Nur Barzahlung'). Always ask beforehand.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich hier mit Karte zahlen?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, ab 10 Euro nehmen wir alle Karten.
dialogue.englishA: Can I pay by card here?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, from 10 euros we take all cards.

german: Nehmen Sie Kreditkarten oder nur EC-Karte?
english: Do you take credit cards or only debit/EC cards?
literalTranslation: Take you credit cards or only EC-card?
situation: Inquiring whether Visa/Mastercard is accepted or only the German Girocard (EC-Karte).
culturalNote: Many small shops in Germany distinguish between Girocard and international credit cards.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich mit Visakarte zahlen?
dialogue.speakerB: Leider nur EC-Karte oder bar.
dialogue.englishA: Can I pay with Visa card?
dialogue.englishB: Unfortunately only EC card or cash.

german: Ich möchte bitte bar bezahlen.
english: I would like to pay in cash, please.
literalTranslation: I would like please cash to pay.
situation: Informing the cashier or server of cash payment.
culturalNote: Cash (Bargeld) remains very popular and respected across Germany.

dialogue.speakerA: Wie möchten Sie bezahlen?
dialogue.speakerB: Ich möchte bitte bar bezahlen.
dialogue.englishA: How would you like to pay?
dialogue.englishB: I would like to pay in cash, please.

german: Haben Sie es passend?
english: Do you have exact change?
literalTranslation: Have you it fitting?
situation: Asked by cashiers when paying with large banknotes.
culturalNote: Cashiers appreciate exact coins ('Kleingeld') especially in smaller bakeries.

dialogue.speakerA: Das macht 3 Euro 20.
dialogue.speakerB: Ich habe nur einen 50-Euro-Schein. - Haben Sie es vielleicht passend?
dialogue.englishA: That's 3.20 euros.
dialogue.englishB: I only have a 50 euro bill. - Do you happen to have exact change?

german: Zum Hieressen oder zum Mitnehmen?
english: For here or to go?
literalTranslation: To here-eat or to take-along?
situation: Standard question at fast food spots, bakeries, and Döner kebabs.
culturalNote: Determines both the packaging and occasionally the VAT rate in Germany (7% takeaway vs 19% dine-in).

dialogue.speakerA: Einen Döner mit allem, bitte.
dialogue.speakerB: Gerne. Zum Hieressen oder zum Mitnehmen?
dialogue.englishA: One Döner with everything, please.
dialogue.englishB: Sure. For here or to go?

german: Zwei Brötchen zum Mitnehmen, bitte.
english: Two bread rolls to go, please.
literalTranslation: Two small breads to take-along, please.
situation: Ordering baked goods at a German bakery (Bäckerei).
culturalNote: Brötchen (or Semmeln in Bavaria/Austria, Schrippen in Berlin) are the cornerstone of German breakfast.

dialogue.speakerA: Guten Morgen! Was darf es sein?
dialogue.speakerB: Zwei Brötchen und ein Croissant zum Mitnehmen, bitte.
dialogue.englishA: Good morning! What can I get for you?
dialogue.englishB: Two bread rolls and a croissant to go, please.

german: Sonst noch ein Wunsch?
english: Anything else you wish? / Anything else for you?
literalTranslation: Otherwise still a wish?
situation: Asked by shop assistants and market vendors when you finish listing items.
culturalNote: Standard retail phrase across German-speaking countries.

dialogue.speakerA: Hier ist Ihr Käse. Sonst noch ein Wunsch?
dialogue.speakerB: Nein danke, das ist alles für heute.
dialogue.englishA: Here is your cheese. Anything else for you?
dialogue.englishB: No thank you, that is all for today.

german: Das wäre alles, danke!
english: That would be all, thanks!
literalTranslation: That would be all, thanks!
situation: Signaling to the shopkeeper or waiter that your order is complete.
culturalNote: Polite and crisp conclusion to ordering.

dialogue.speakerA: Brauchen Sie noch etwas?
dialogue.speakerB: Nein, das wäre alles, danke!
dialogue.englishA: Do you need anything else?
dialogue.englishB: No, that would be all, thanks!

german: Schönen Feierabend!
english: Have a great evening after work!
literalTranslation: Beautiful celebration-evening!
situation: Wishing colleagues or shopkeepers a pleasant time at the end of their workday.
culturalNote: Feierabend is a cherished German cultural concept denoting the sacred transition from work hours to personal leisure time.

dialogue.speakerA: Ich mache jetzt Schluss für heute. Bis morgen!
dialogue.speakerB: Schönen Feierabend! Ruh dich gut aus.
dialogue.englishA: I'm wrapping up for today. See you tomorrow!
dialogue.englishB: Have a great evening after work! Rest well.

german: Danke, gleichfalls! / Ebenso!
english: Thank you, same to you! / Likewise!
literalTranslation: Thanks, equal-case! / As-well!
situation: The universal response to any friendly wish (weekend, meal, evening, vacation).
culturalNote: Short, polite, and universally applicable in both formal and casual settings.

dialogue.speakerA: Schönes Wochenende!
dialogue.speakerB: Danke, gleichfalls!
dialogue.englishA: Have a nice weekend!
dialogue.englishB: Thank you, same to you!

german: Dir auch! / Ihnen auch!
english: To you too! (informal / formal)
literalTranslation: To you also!
situation: Friendly reply returning a good wish.
culturalNote: Use 'Dir auch' with friends and 'Ihnen auch' with strangers, bosses, or cashiers.

dialogue.speakerA: Guten Appetit beim Mittagessen!
dialogue.speakerB: Danke, dir auch!
dialogue.englishA: Enjoy your lunch!
dialogue.englishB: Thanks, you too!

german: Wie läuft's bei dir?
english: How's it going with you? / How are things?
literalTranslation: How runs it by you?
situation: Casual inquiry into a friend or colleague's current life or work situation.
culturalNote: More conversational and natural than textbook 'Wie geht es Ihnen?'.

dialogue.speakerA: Hey Jan! Lange nicht gesehen, wie läuft's bei dir?
dialogue.speakerB: Alles bestens! Neuer Job, neue Wohnung.
dialogue.englishA: Hey Jan! Long time no see, how are things going with you?
dialogue.englishB: Everything great! New job, new apartment.

german: Alles im grünen Bereich.
english: Everything is in the green zone / all is well.
literalTranslation: Everything in the green area.
situation: Reassuring someone that everything is running smoothly and under control.
culturalNote: Comes from gauge needles pointing to the safe green zone on machinery meters.

dialogue.speakerA: Gibt es Probleme mit dem Projekt?
dialogue.speakerB: Nein, keine Sorge, alles im grünen Bereich!
dialogue.englishA: Are there problems with the project?
dialogue.englishB: No, no worries, everything is well under control!

german: Muss ja!
english: Gotta keep going! / Can't complain (pragmatic).
literalTranslation: Must indeed!
situation: Quintessential pragmatic North/Central German reply to 'Wie geht's?'.
culturalNote: Reflects a typical German understated realism: 'Life goes on, doing what needs to be done.'

dialogue.speakerA: Hallo Klaus, wie geht's?
dialogue.speakerB: Ach, muss ja! Und bei dir?
dialogue.englishA: Hello Klaus, how's it going?
dialogue.englishB: Ah, gotta keep going! And with you?

german: Mach's gut! - Mach's besser!
english: Take care! - (Humorous reply) You do better!
literalTranslation: Make it good! - Make it better!
situation: Warm casual farewell between good friends.
culturalNote: 'Mach's gut' is widely used when parting ways with friends after meeting up.

dialogue.speakerA: Ich muss jetzt zur Bahn. Mach's gut!
dialogue.speakerB: Tschüss, mach's besser!
dialogue.englishA: I have to get to the train now. Take care!
dialogue.englishB: Bye, you take care too!

german: Pass auf dich auf!
english: Take care of yourself! / Stay safe!
literalTranslation: Watch onto yourself on!
situation: Caring wish when saying goodbye to someone embarking on a journey or facing hardship.
culturalNote: Shows warm personal empathy and care.

dialogue.speakerA: Gute Reise nach Berlin! Pass gut auf dich auf.
dialogue.speakerB: Vielen Dank, ich melde mich sobald ich ankomme.
dialogue.englishA: Have a good trip to Berlin! Take good care of yourself.
dialogue.englishB: Thank you very much, I'll check in as soon as I arrive.

german: Lange nicht gesehen!
english: Long time no see!
literalTranslation: Long not seen!
situation: Said when bumping into an acquaintance or friend you haven't crossed paths with in a while.
culturalNote: Warmly breaks the ice and prompts catching up.

dialogue.speakerA: Mensch Anna! Lange nicht gesehen!
dialogue.speakerB: Hallo Thomas! Ja, bestimmt schon ein ganzes Jahr!
dialogue.englishA: Man Anna! Long time no see!
dialogue.englishB: Hello Thomas! Yes, definitely a whole year!

german: Was gibt's Neues?
english: What's new? / What's the news?
literalTranslation: What gives it of new?
situation: Prompting a friend to share recent life updates or gossip.
culturalNote: Common conversational starter during coffee or beer meetups.

dialogue.speakerA: Erzähl mal, was gibt's Neues bei dir?
dialogue.speakerB: Ich habe mir letzte Woche einen Hund geholt!
dialogue.englishA: Tell me, what's new with you?
dialogue.englishB: I got myself a dog last week!

german: Man sieht sich!
english: See you around! / Catch you later!
literalTranslation: One sees oneself!
situation: Casual, relaxed way of saying goodbye to acquaintances or coworkers.
culturalNote: Implies you will naturally run into each other again soon.

dialogue.speakerA: Ich gehe jetzt zum Training. Bis dann!
dialogue.speakerB: Alles klar, man sieht sich!
dialogue.englishA: I'm heading to practice now. See you then!
dialogue.englishB: All right, see you around!

german: Bis die Tage!
english: See you in the next few days / See you soon!
literalTranslation: Until the days!
situation: Colloquial German parting phrase when you expect to meet in the near future.
culturalNote: Very popular in western and central German spoken dialects.

dialogue.speakerA: Danke für den netten Abend!
dialogue.speakerB: Gerne wieder, bis die Tage!
dialogue.englishA: Thanks for the pleasant evening!
dialogue.englishB: Gladly again, see you in the coming days!

german: Schönes Wochenende!
english: Have a nice weekend!
literalTranslation: Beautiful weekend!
situation: Standard farewell on Friday afternoon or evening to anyone.
culturalNote: Universally used by cashiers, colleagues, teachers, and neighbors.

dialogue.speakerA: Ich bin dann weg. Schönes Wochenende allerseits!
dialogue.speakerB: Danke, dir auch ein erholsames Wochenende!
dialogue.englishA: I'm off then. Have a nice weekend everyone!
dialogue.englishB: Thanks, you also have a restful weekend!

german: Erhol dich gut!
english: Get some good rest! / Relax well!
literalTranslation: Recover yourself well!
situation: Wishing someone a refreshing rest over the weekend, holiday, or vacation.
culturalNote: Highlights the value Germans place on proper rest and recovery (Erholung).

dialogue.speakerA: Ich habe zwei Wochen Urlaub.
dialogue.speakerB: Das hast du dir verdient! Erhol dich gut!
dialogue.englishA: I have two weeks of vacation.
dialogue.englishB: You've earned that! Rest well and enjoy!

german: Was machst du am Wochenende so?
english: What are you up to this weekend?
literalTranslation: What do you on the weekend so?
situation: Inquiring about someone's leisure plans for Saturday/Sunday.
culturalNote: Classic Friday conversation starter at work or school.

dialogue.speakerA: Was machst du am Wochenende so?
dialogue.speakerB: Wenn das Wetter schön ist, fahre ich an den See.
dialogue.englishA: What are you doing this weekend?
dialogue.englishB: If the weather is nice, I'm heading to the lake.

german: Das Wetter spielt heute leider nicht mit.
english: The weather isn't playing along today, unfortunately. / Bad weather.
literalTranslation: The weather plays today unfortunately not with.
situation: Commenting when rain or cold ruins outdoor plans.
culturalNote: A staple idiom for German small talk about the climate.

dialogue.speakerA: Wollten wir nicht grillen?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, aber das Wetter spielt heute leider nicht mit.
dialogue.englishA: Weren't we going to barbecue?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, but the weather isn't playing along today unfortunately.

german: Es regnet wie aus Eimern!
english: It's pouring buckets! / Raining cats and dogs!
literalTranslation: It rains like out-of buckets!
situation: Describing torrential downpours.
culturalNote: Direct counterpart to the English 'raining cats and dogs'.

dialogue.speakerA: Hast du einen Regenschirm dabei?
dialogue.speakerB: Nein, und es regnet wie aus Eimern!
dialogue.englishA: Do you have an umbrella with you?
dialogue.englishB: No, and it's pouring buckets!

german: Schönes Wetter heute, nicht wahr?
english: Beautiful weather today, isn't it?
literalTranslation: Beautiful weather today, not true?
situation: Classic ice-breaker when standing at a bus stop or in an elevator.
culturalNote: Safe, universally understood small-talk starter.

dialogue.speakerA: Schönes Wetter heute, nicht wahr?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, herrlicher Sonnenschein nach der langen Kälte!
dialogue.englishA: Beautiful weather today, isn't it?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, glorious sunshine after the long cold!

german: Ich schaue mich nur um, danke.
english: I'm just looking around, thank you.
literalTranslation: I look myself only around, thanks.
situation: Politely declining immediate assistance from a shop attendant while browsing.
culturalNote: Attendants in Germany will say 'Sagen Sie Bescheid, wenn Sie Hilfe brauchen' (Let me know if you need help) and leave you to browse in peace.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen helfen?
dialogue.speakerB: Vielen Dank, ich schaue mich nur um.
dialogue.englishA: Can I help you?
dialogue.englishB: Thank you very much, I'm just looking around.

relatedPhrases: Ich melde mich, wenn ich Fragen habe.

german: Brauchen Sie den Kassenbon / Beleg?
english: Do you need the receipt?
literalTranslation: Need you the cash-slip / voucher?
situation: Asked by cashiers at the register after completing payment.
culturalNote: In Germany (due to receipt obligation laws / Bonpflicht), cashiers must generate a receipt and ask if you want to take it.

dialogue.speakerA: Das macht 14 Euro 20. Brauchen Sie den Beleg?
dialogue.speakerB: Nein danke, den können Sie wegwerfen.
dialogue.englishA: That's 14.20 euros. Do you need the receipt?
dialogue.englishB: No thank you, you can throw it away.

german: Haben Sie das auch in einer anderen Größe?
english: Do you have this in a different size too?
literalTranslation: Have you that also in an other size?
situation: Asking a clothing store assistant for size adjustments (S, M, L, XL).
culturalNote: Standard retail question when trying on clothes in changing rooms.

dialogue.speakerA: Die Jacke gefällt mir, aber sie ist zu klein. Haben Sie Größe L?
dialogue.speakerB: Ich schaue gerne im Lager für Sie nach.
dialogue.englishA: I like the jacket, but it's too small. Do you have size L?
dialogue.englishB: I'll gladly check in the stockroom for you.

german: Wo sind die Umkleidekabinen?
english: Where are the fitting rooms / changing rooms?
literalTranslation: Where are the dressing-cabins?
situation: Locating the changing cubicles in clothing stores.
culturalNote: Usually located towards the back of the store.

dialogue.speakerA: Entschuldigung, wo sind die Umkleidekabinen?
dialogue.speakerB: Gleich dort hinten links neben den Spiegeln.
dialogue.englishA: Excuse me, where are the fitting rooms?
dialogue.englishB: Right back there on the left next to the mirrors.

german: Kann ich das anprobieren?
english: Can I try this on?
literalTranslation: Can I that on-try?
situation: Asking permission to try on a garment or accessory before buying.
culturalNote: Standard etiquette in clothing boutiques.

dialogue.speakerA: Das Hemd sieht toll aus. Kann ich das anprobieren?
dialogue.speakerB: Selbstverständlich, die Kabinen sind dort drüben.
dialogue.englishA: The shirt looks great. Can I try this on?
dialogue.englishB: Of course, the cabins are over there.

german: Das steht dir ausgezeichnet!
english: That looks fantastic on you! / That suits you wonderfully!
literalTranslation: That stands to-you excellent!
situation: Complimenting someone on an outfit, haircut, or accessory.
culturalNote: 'Jemandem stehen' is the idiomatic German construction for clothing suiting someone.

dialogue.speakerA: Wie gefällt dir das Kleid an mir?
dialogue.speakerB: Wow, das steht dir wirklich ausgezeichnet!
dialogue.englishA: How do you like the dress on me?
dialogue.englishB: Wow, that suits you really excellently!

german: Das passt wie angegossen!
english: It fits like a glove!
literalTranslation: That fits like cast-on!
situation: Describing a piece of clothing that fits perfectly without needing tailoring.
culturalNote: German idiom derived from molten metal fitting into a mold.

dialogue.speakerA: Sitzt die Hose bequem?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, sie passt wie angegossen!
dialogue.englishA: Does the pair of pants sit comfortably?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, it fits like a glove!

german: Kann ich das umtauschen, falls es nicht passt?
english: Can I exchange this if it doesn't fit?
literalTranslation: Can I that exchange, in-case it not fits?
situation: Checking return and exchange policies before buying gifts.
culturalNote: Usually requires keeping the receipt (Kassenbon) intact with original tags.

dialogue.speakerA: Das ist ein Geschenk für meinen Bruder. Kann ich es umtauschen?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, innerhalb von 14 Tagen mit Kassenbon.
dialogue.englishA: This is a gift for my brother. Can I exchange it?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, within 14 days with the receipt.

german: Ich möchte das gerne reklamieren.
english: I would like to make a formal complaint / return for defect.
literalTranslation: I would like that gladly to-complain.
situation: Returning a defective or damaged product under statutory warranty (Gewährleistung).
culturalNote: In Germany, consumer rights strongly protect against faulty products within 24 months.

dialogue.speakerA: Guten Tag, das Gerät funktioniert leider nicht mehr. Ich möchte es reklamieren.
dialogue.speakerB: Haben Sie die Rechnung dabei? Wir reparieren es oder tauschen es aus.
dialogue.englishA: Good day, the device unfortunately no longer works. I'd like to return it under warranty.
dialogue.englishB: Do you have the invoice with you? We will repair or replace it.

german: Ist dieses Produkt im Angebot?
english: Is this product on sale / on special offer?
literalTranslation: Is this product in the offer?
situation: Asking if an item has a discounted promotional price.
culturalNote: Supermarket circulars in Germany are called 'Angebote der Woche'.

dialogue.speakerA: Entschuldigung, ist dieser Kaffee heute im Angebot?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, er kostet diese Woche nur 4 Euro 99.
dialogue.englishA: Excuse me, is this coffee on special offer today?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, it costs only 4.99 euros this week.

german: Darf ich mal kurz vorbei?
english: May I briefly squeeze past? / Excuse me (in aisle).
literalTranslation: May I once short past?
situation: Politely asking someone blocking the supermarket aisle or doorway to step aside.
culturalNote: Short, friendly, and essential in crowded grocery aisles.

dialogue.speakerA: Entschuldigung, darf ich mal kurz vorbei?
dialogue.speakerB: Oh, Verzeihung! Natürlich.
dialogue.englishA: Excuse me, may I just squeeze past?
dialogue.englishB: Oh, pardon! Of course.

german: Sammeln Sie Treuepunkte?
english: Do you collect loyalty points / stamps?
literalTranslation: Collect you loyalty-points?
situation: Asked at supermarket checkout (Payback / supermarket stamps).
culturalNote: The Payback card system is immensely popular across German retail chains.

dialogue.speakerA: Das macht 32 Euro. Sammeln Sie Payback-Punkte?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, hier ist meine Karte.
dialogue.englishA: That's 32 euros. Do you collect Payback points?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, here is my card.

german: Brauchen Sie eine Tüte?
english: Do you need a shopping bag?
literalTranslation: Need you a bag?
situation: Asked by the cashier at checkout.
culturalNote: In Germany, single-use bags are not free; customers bring reusable tote bags (Stoffbeutel) or pay a small fee per paper bag.

dialogue.speakerA: Brauchen Sie eine Tüte dazu?
dialogue.speakerB: Nein danke, ich habe einen Stoffbeutel mitgebracht.
dialogue.englishA: Do you need a bag with that?
dialogue.englishB: No thank you, I brought a cloth tote bag.

german: Pfand gehört daneben!
english: Leave the refundable bottle next to the bin! (Berlin street culture).
literalTranslation: Deposit belongs next-to!
situation: German cultural norm of leaving returnable bottles next to public trash bins so collectors can retrieve deposit money safely.
culturalNote: Germany's Pfand system refunds 0.08€ to 0.25€ per bottle. Leaving them beside bins aids bottle collectors (Pfandsammler).

dialogue.speakerA: Soll ich die Glasflasche in den Mülleimer werfen?
dialogue.speakerB: Nein, stell sie unten hin – Pfand gehört daneben!
dialogue.englishA: Should I throw the glass bottle in the trash can?
dialogue.englishB: No, place it on the ground – deposit bottles belong next to the bin!

german: Entschuldigung, wie komme ich zum Hauptbahnhof?
english: Excuse me, how do I get to the central train station?
literalTranslation: Excuse, how come I to the main-train-station?
situation: Asking pedestrians for directions to the primary railway station in a city.
culturalNote: Every major German city's central transit hub is called the 'Hauptbahnhof' (Hbf).

dialogue.speakerA: Entschuldigung, wie komme ich zum Hauptbahnhof?
dialogue.speakerB: Gehen Sie einfach geradeaus und dann die zweite Straße rechts.
dialogue.englishA: Excuse me, how do I get to the central station?
dialogue.englishB: Just go straight ahead and then take the second street on the right.

german: Fährt dieser Zug nach Frankfurt?
english: Does this train go to Frankfurt?
literalTranslation: Drives this train to Frankfurt?
situation: Confirming train destination with conductors or fellow passengers on the platform.
culturalNote: Double-checking is helpful because long-distance ICE trains sometimes decouple into two separate destinations at junction stations (Flügelung).

dialogue.speakerA: Entschuldigung, fährt dieser Zug nach Frankfurt?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, das ist der ICE nach Frankfurt über Mannheim.
dialogue.englishA: Excuse me, does this train go to Frankfurt?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, this is the ICE to Frankfurt via Mannheim.

relatedPhrases: Auf welchem Gleis fährt der Zug?

german: Auf welchem Gleis fährt der Zug ab?
english: Which platform does the train depart from?
literalTranslation: On which track drives the train off?
situation: Asking station staff for track numbers (Gleis).
culturalNote: Platform changes (Gleiswechsel) are announced over station loudspeakers.

dialogue.speakerA: Verzeihung, auf welchem Gleis fährt der Zug nach Hamburg?
dialogue.speakerB: Heute von Gleis 7 statt Gleis 4.
dialogue.englishA: Pardon, which track does the train to Hamburg depart from?
dialogue.englishB: Today from track 7 instead of track 4.

german: Der Zug hat heute 15 Minuten Verspätung.
english: The train is 15 minutes delayed today.
literalTranslation: The train has today 15 minutes delay.
situation: Classic Deutsche Bahn announcement phrase regarding schedule delays.
culturalNote: A frequent talking point and meme among German travelers.

dialogue.speakerA: Wann kommt unser Zug?
dialogue.speakerB: Auf der Anzeigetafel steht: 15 Minuten Verspätung.
dialogue.englishA: When is our train coming?
dialogue.englishB: The display board says: 15 minutes delay.

german: Wo muss ich umsteigen?
english: Where do I have to transfer / change trains?
literalTranslation: Where must I around-climb?
situation: Asking for transit transfer stations.
culturalNote: Umsteigen = change train/bus; Einsteigen = board; Aussteigen = alight.

dialogue.speakerA: Muss ich direkt fahren oder umsteigen?
dialogue.speakerB: Sie müssen in Köln Hauptbahnhof auf Gleis 9 umsteigen.
dialogue.englishA: Do I ride direct or transfer?
dialogue.englishB: You have to transfer at Cologne Central Station on track 9.

german: Einfach oder hin und zurück?
english: One-way or round-trip?
literalTranslation: Simple or there and back?
situation: Asked at ticket counters when purchasing train or bus tickets.
culturalNote: 'Einfache Fahrt' = one-way ticket; 'Hin- und Rückfahrt' = round-trip ticket.

dialogue.speakerA: Ich möchte eine Fahrkarte nach Stuttgart, bitte.
dialogue.speakerB: Gerne. Einfach oder hin und zurück?
dialogue.englishA: I would like a ticket to Stuttgart, please.
dialogue.englishB: Certainly. One-way or round-trip?

german: Haben Sie eine BahnCard?
english: Do you have a BahnCard (discount discount card)?
literalTranslation: Have you a BahnCard?
situation: Asked at Deutsche Bahn counters or ticket machines.
culturalNote: The BahnCard 25 and BahnCard 50 offer 25% or 50% discounts on German train tickets.

dialogue.speakerA: Eine Fahrkarte nach München, bitte.
dialogue.speakerB: Haben Sie eine BahnCard 25 oder 50?
dialogue.englishA: A ticket to Munich, please.
dialogue.englishB: Do you have a BahnCard 25 or 50?

german: Gilt hier das Deutschlandticket?
english: Is the Deutschlandticket (49€ ticket) valid here?
literalTranslation: Applies here the Germany-ticket?
situation: Checking ticket validity on regional transport lines.
culturalNote: The Deutschlandticket is valid on all local and regional trains (RB, RE, S-Bahn, U-Bahn, Bus, Tram) but NOT on long-distance ICE/IC trains.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich mit dem Deutschlandticket in diesen Zug einsteigen?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, in alle Regionalbahnen (RE und RB)!
dialogue.englishA: Can I board this train with the Deutschlandticket?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, in all regional trains (RE and RB)!

german: Zurückbleiben, bitte!
english: Stand back, please! / Stand clear of the doors!
literalTranslation: Back-stay, please!
situation: Automated announcement on German U-Bahn and S-Bahn platforms before doors close.
culturalNote: Signals that doors are closing immediately and boarding is no longer allowed.

dialogue.speakerA: Der Zug fährt gleich ab. Zurückbleiben, bitte!
dialogue.speakerB: Vorsicht bei der Abfahrt!
dialogue.englishA: The train is about to depart. Stand clear, please!
dialogue.englishB: Caution during departure!

german: Die Fahrscheine, bitte!
english: Tickets, please! / Ticket inspection!
literalTranslation: The ride-slips, please!
situation: Announced by plainclothes or uniformed ticket inspectors (Kontrolleure).
culturalNote: Riding without a valid stamped ticket (Schwarzfahren) results in a 60€ penalty fine in Germany.

dialogue.speakerA: Guten Tag, die Fahrscheine bitte zur Kontrolle!
dialogue.speakerB: Hier ist mein digitales Ticket auf dem Handy.
dialogue.englishA: Good day, tickets please for inspection!
dialogue.englishB: Here is my digital ticket on my phone.

german: Muss ich das Ticket noch entwerten?
english: Do I still need to validate/stamp this ticket?
literalTranslation: Must I the ticket still un-value?
situation: Checking if a paper transit ticket needs stamping in the little box validator before boarding.
culturalNote: In many German transit networks (MVV, BVG, VVS), unstamped paper tickets are considered invalid.

dialogue.speakerA: Ich habe das Ticket am Automaten gekauft. Muss ich es entwerten?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, bitte am gelben Kasten auf dem Bahnsteig abstempeln.
dialogue.englishA: I bought the ticket at the machine. Do I need to validate it?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, please stamp it at the yellow box on the platform.

german: Halt auf Verlangen.
english: Stop on request.
literalTranslation: Hold on demand.
situation: Appears on bus display screens indicating you must push the red stop button to alight.
culturalNote: Buses in rural German areas will pass stops unless someone rings the bell.

dialogue.speakerA: Nächste Haltestelle: Waldstraße. Halt auf Verlangen.
dialogue.speakerB: Ich drücke schnell den Halt-Knopf!
dialogue.englishA: Next stop: Waldstraße. Stop on request.
dialogue.englishB: I'll quickly press the stop button!

german: Können wir das kurz besprechen?
english: Could we briefly discuss this?
literalTranslation: Can we that short discuss?
situation: Requesting a quick 5-minute alignment with a manager or colleague.
culturalNote: Common polite formula in German office environments.

dialogue.speakerA: Hast du zwei Minuten Zeit? Können wir das kurz besprechen?
dialogue.speakerB: Klar, komm kurz an meinen Schreibtisch rüber.
dialogue.englishA: Do you have two minutes? Could we briefly discuss this?
dialogue.englishB: Sure, come over to my desk for a second.

german: Ich gebe Ihnen Bescheid.
english: I will let you know. / I will inform you.
literalTranslation: I give to-you decision/notice.
situation: Promising to send an update once information is confirmed.
culturalNote: Ubiquitous in German business emails and phone calls ('Bescheid geben / Bescheid sagen').

dialogue.speakerA: Wann wissen wir das Ergebnis?
dialogue.speakerB: Ich prüfe das und gebe Ihnen heute Nachmittag Bescheid.
dialogue.englishA: When will we know the result?
dialogue.englishB: I'll check that and let you know this afternoon.

relatedPhrases: Ich halte Sie auf dem Laufenden.

german: Ich halte Sie auf dem Laufenden.
english: I will keep you posted / updated.
literalTranslation: I hold you on the running.
situation: Assuring someone they will receive continuous updates on an ongoing situation.
culturalNote: Polite professional closing line in business correspondence.

dialogue.speakerA: Vielen Dank für die Auskunft.
dialogue.speakerB: Sehr gerne, ich halte Sie auf dem Laufenden!
dialogue.englishA: Thank you very much for the information.
dialogue.englishB: Very gladly, I will keep you updated!

german: Lass uns das vertagen.
english: Let's postpone / table this for later.
literalTranslation: Let us that adjourn.
situation: Suggesting moving an unresolved discussion to a future meeting.
culturalNote: Standard boardroom and meeting terminology in Germany.

dialogue.speakerA: Wir drehen uns im Kreis. Lass uns das auf nächste Woche vertagen.
dialogue.speakerB: Gute Idee, dann sammeln wir bis dahin mehr Daten.
dialogue.englishA: We are going in circles. Let's table this until next week.
dialogue.englishB: Good idea, we'll gather more data until then.

german: Ich bin gleich wieder da.
english: I will be right back.
literalTranslation: I am equal again there.
situation: Excusing yourself for 1-2 minutes from a meeting or desk.
culturalNote: Polite and concise.

dialogue.speakerA: Entschuldigung, das Telefon klingelt. Ich bin gleich wieder da!
dialogue.speakerB: Kein Problem, nimm dir Zeit.
dialogue.englishA: Excuse me, the phone is ringing. I'll be right back!
dialogue.englishB: No problem, take your time.

german: Mahlzeit!
english: Mealtime! / Enjoy your lunch break! / Midday greeting.
literalTranslation: Meal-time!
situation: The iconic German workplace greeting between 11:30 AM and 2:00 PM in office hallways and canteen.
culturalNote: Serves simultaneously as a greeting, an acknowledgment of lunchtime, and wishing 'Guten Appetit'.

dialogue.speakerA: Mahlzeit, Herr Müller! Gehen Sie auch in die Kantine?
dialogue.speakerB: Mahlzeit! Ja, heute gibt es Currywurst.
dialogue.englishA: Mahlzeit, Mr. Müller! Are you heading to the canteen too?
dialogue.englishB: Mahlzeit! Yes, today they have currywurst.

german: Schöne Mittagspause!
english: Have a nice lunch break!
literalTranslation: Beautiful midday-break!
situation: Wishing coworkers a pleasant break as they head out to eat.
culturalNote: German labor law strictly regulates lunch breaks (Pause).

dialogue.speakerA: Wir gehen jetzt essen. Bis später!
dialogue.speakerB: Lasst es euch schmecken und schöne Mittagspause!
dialogue.englishA: We're going to eat now. See you later!
dialogue.englishB: Enjoy your food and have a nice lunch break!

german: Das liegt nicht in meinem Zuständigkeitsbereich.
english: That is not within my area of responsibility.
literalTranslation: That lies not in my responsibility-sphere.
situation: Explaining politely that another department or colleague handles this matter.
culturalNote: Very common in German corporate and bureaucratic institutions (Zuständigkeit).

dialogue.speakerA: Können Sie meinen Urlaubsantrag genehmigen?
dialogue.speakerB: Das liegt leider nicht in meinem Zuständigkeitsbereich, bitte wenden Sie sich an die Personalabteilung.
dialogue.englishA: Can you approve my vacation request?
dialogue.englishB: That is unfortunately not within my area of responsibility; please contact HR.

relatedPhrases: Wenden Sie sich an die Kollegen.

german: Ich habe mich krankgemeldet.
english: I called in sick / reported off sick.
literalTranslation: I have myself sick-reported.
situation: Informing colleagues or employer of illness.
culturalNote: In Germany, an official doctor's note for sick leave is called an 'Arbeitsunfähigkeitsbescheinigung' (AU) or 'Krankschreibung'.

dialogue.speakerA: Wo ist Stefan heute?
dialogue.speakerB: Er hat sich für heute und morgen krankgemeldet.
dialogue.englishA: Where is Stefan today?
dialogue.englishB: He called in sick for today and tomorrow.

german: Ich verstehe nur Bahnhof.
english: It's all Greek to me. / I don't understand a thing.
literalTranslation: I understand only train-station.
situation: Admitting that you have completely failed to comprehend what was just said.
culturalNote: Originated among WW1 soldiers who were so tired of war that all they wanted to hear was 'Bahnhof' (the train station to go home).

dialogue.speakerA: Hast du die Quantenphysik-Vorlesung verstanden?
dialogue.speakerB: Ehrlich gesagt verstehe ich nur Bahnhof!
dialogue.englishA: Did you understand the quantum physics lecture?
dialogue.englishB: To be honest, it's all Greek to me!

german: Ich drücke dir die Daumen!
english: I'm crossing my fingers for you! / Wishing you luck!
literalTranslation: I press to-you the thumbs!
situation: Wishing someone success in an exam, interview, or challenge.
culturalNote: Germans press their thumbs inside their fists ('Daumen drücken') rather than crossing their fingers.

dialogue.speakerA: Morgen habe ich meine Führerscheinprüfung.
dialogue.speakerB: Ich drücke dir ganz fest die Daumen!
dialogue.englishA: Tomorrow I have my driving test.
dialogue.englishB: I'll cross my fingers tightly for you!

german: Das ist mir Wurst / Wurscht!
english: I couldn't care less! / It doesn't matter to me at all!
literalTranslation: That is to-me sausage!
situation: Expressing complete indifference between two choices.
culturalNote: Derived from the fact that in a sausage (Wurst), all leftover ingredients end up mixed together anyway.

dialogue.speakerA: Möchtest du heute lieber Pizza oder Pasta?
dialogue.speakerB: Das ist mir völlig Wurst, such du aus!
dialogue.englishA: Would you prefer pizza or pasta today?
dialogue.englishB: I don't care at all, you pick!

german: Schwein gehabt!
english: Had a stroke of good luck! / Got lucky!
literalTranslation: Pig had!
situation: Said when you narrowly escaped a bad outcome or had unexpected good luck.
culturalNote: In medieval shooting competitions, the loser who hit nothing was given a pig as a consolation prize, unexpectedly receiving valuable food.

dialogue.speakerA: Fast hätte mich der Blitzer erwischt!
dialogue.speakerB: Da hast du aber echt Schwein gehabt!
dialogue.englishA: The speed camera almost caught me!
dialogue.englishB: You really had a lucky break there!

german: Ich habe den Faden verloren.
english: I lost my train of thought.
literalTranslation: I have the thread lost.
situation: Said during a speech or conversation when you forget what you were going to say next.
culturalNote: Refers to Ariadne's thread in ancient mythology or spinning threads in weaving.

dialogue.speakerA: Wo war ich gerade stehen geblieben? Ich habe den Faden verloren.
dialogue.speakerB: Du hast von deinem Urlaub in Italien erzählt.
dialogue.englishA: Where was I just now? I lost my train of thought.
dialogue.englishB: You were talking about your vacation in Italy.

relatedPhrases: Mir fällt das Wort nicht ein.

german: Das ist nicht das Gelbe vom Ei.
english: That's not the greatest / not optimal / leaves much to be desired.
literalTranslation: That is not the yellow of-the egg.
situation: Critiquing a solution or product as mediocre or substandard.
culturalNote: The egg yolk (das Gelbe) is traditionally considered the tastiest, richest part of the egg.

dialogue.speakerA: Wie gefällt dir das neue Design?
dialogue.speakerB: Naja, es funktioniert, aber das Gelbe vom Ei ist es nicht.
dialogue.englishA: How do you like the new design?
dialogue.englishB: Well, it works, but it's not the greatest.

relatedPhrases: Da ist noch Luft nach oben.

german: Ins Fettnäpfchen treten.
english: To put your foot in your mouth / commit a social faux pas.
literalTranslation: Into-the grease-pot to-step.
situation: Accidentally making an embarrassing or tactless remark.
culturalNote: Historically, a grease bowl was kept near the hearth to grease boots, and stepping into it made a messy grease stain on clean floors.

dialogue.speakerA: Warum ist Lisa so sauer?
dialogue.speakerB: Ich habe sie gefragt, ob sie schwanger ist – da bin ich voll ins Fettnäpfchen getreten!
dialogue.englishA: Why is Lisa so angry?
dialogue.englishB: I asked if she was pregnant – I really put my foot in my mouth!

german: Zwei Fliegen mit einer Klappe schlagen.
english: To kill two birds with one stone.
literalTranslation: Two flies with one swatter to-hit.
situation: Accomplishing two objectives with a single action.
culturalNote: Direct German counterpart using flies and a flyswatter.

dialogue.speakerA: Wenn wir auf dem Rückweg einkaufen, schlagen wir zwei Fliegen mit einer Klappe.
dialogue.speakerB: Super Idee, das spart uns eine Extrafahrt!
dialogue.englishA: If we grocery shop on the way back, we kill two birds with one stone.
dialogue.englishB: Great idea, that saves us an extra trip!

german: Die Daumen drücken.
english: To keep one's fingers crossed.
literalTranslation: The thumbs to-press.
situation: Wishing someone good fortune.
culturalNote: Physical gesture in Germany where thumbs are tucked under closed fingers.

dialogue.speakerA: Ich habe gleich das Bewerbungsgespräch.
dialogue.speakerB: Ich drücke dir ganz fest die Daumen!
dialogue.englishA: I have my job interview in a moment.
dialogue.englishB: I'm crossing my fingers tightly for you!

german: Halt die Ohren steif!
english: Keep your chin up! / Stay strong!
literalTranslation: Hold the ears stiff!
situation: Encouraging someone who is going through a difficult or stressful period.
culturalNote: Comes from animals perking up their ears to stay alert and confident.

dialogue.speakerA: Die Prüfungsphase ist echt anstrengend.
dialogue.speakerB: Kopf hoch und halt die Ohren steif! Bald ist es vorbei.
dialogue.englishA: The exam period is really exhausting.
dialogue.englishB: Chin up and keep your chin up! It will be over soon.

german: Lass dich nicht unterkriegen!
english: Don't let it get you down! / Don't let them beat you!
literalTranslation: Let yourself not down-get!
situation: Motivational encouragement when someone faces setbacks.
culturalNote: Strong message of perseverance and resilience.

dialogue.speakerA: Mein Antrag wurde leider abgelehnt.
dialogue.speakerB: Lass dich nicht unterkriegen, wir legen Widerspruch ein!
dialogue.englishA: My application was unfortunately rejected.
dialogue.englishB: Don't let it get you down, we'll file an appeal!

german: Tomaten auf den Augen haben.
english: To be blind to what's right in front of you.
literalTranslation: Tomatoes on the eyes to-have.
situation: Said when someone overlooks an obvious object right before their eyes.
culturalNote: Playful German teasing for temporary blindness to things.

dialogue.speakerA: Wo ist denn mein Schlüssel?
dialogue.speakerB: Der liegt direkt vor dir! Hast du Tomaten auf den Augen?
dialogue.englishA: Where on earth are my keys?
dialogue.englishB: They're right in front of you! Do you have tomatoes on your eyes?

german: Den Nagel auf den Kopf treffen.
english: To hit the nail right on the head.
literalTranslation: The nail onto the head to-hit.
situation: Stating exactly what is true or identifying the core problem perfectly.
culturalNote: Universal carpentry metaphor common across Germanic languages.

dialogue.speakerA: Das Problem ist mangelnde Kommunikation im Team.
dialogue.speakerB: Genau damit hast du den Nagel auf den Kopf getroffen!
dialogue.englishA: The problem is lack of communication in the team.
dialogue.englishB: With that, you have hit the nail right on the head!

german: Gute Besserung!
english: Get well soon!
literalTranslation: Good improvement/bettering!
situation: Wishing a sick or recovering person a speedy recovery.
culturalNote: The standard compassionate phrase when hearing someone is ill.

dialogue.speakerA: Ich liege mit Grippe im Bett.
dialogue.speakerB: Oh je, gute Besserung! Trink viel Tee.
dialogue.englishA: I'm in bed with the flu.
dialogue.englishB: Oh dear, get well soon! Drink lots of tea.

german: Viel Erfolg!
english: Much success! / Best of luck!
literalTranslation: Much success!
situation: Wishing someone success on a business project, test, or endeavor where effort is involved.
culturalNote: Germans distinguish between 'Viel Glück' (pure chance/lottery) and 'Viel Erfolg' (earned achievement/exams).

dialogue.speakerA: Ich halte gleich die Präsentation vor dem Vorstand.
dialogue.speakerB: Viel Erfolg! Du bist bestens vorbereitet.
dialogue.englishA: I'm holding the presentation before the board in a moment.
dialogue.englishB: Much success! You are perfectly prepared.

german: Nicht der Rede wert!
english: Don't mention it! / Not worth mentioning!
literalTranslation: Not of-the speech worth!
situation: Modestly dismissing a thank you for a small favor.
culturalNote: Equivalent to 'No problem at all' or 'Glad to help'.

dialogue.speakerA: Vielen Dank, dass du mir beim Tragen geholfen hast!
dialogue.speakerB: Gerne geschehen, nicht der Rede wert!
dialogue.englishA: Thank you so much for helping me carry!
dialogue.englishB: You're welcome, don't mention it!

german: Gern geschehen! / Keine Ursache!
english: You're welcome! / Don't mention it!
literalTranslation: Gladly happened! / No cause!
situation: Polite response to 'Danke schön'.
culturalNote: Universally used across Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

dialogue.speakerA: Danke für deine Unterstützung!
dialogue.speakerB: Gern geschehen! Jederzeit wieder.
dialogue.englishA: Thanks for your support!
dialogue.englishB: You're welcome! Anytime again.

german: Keine Ahnung.
english: No idea. / I have no clue.
literalTranslation: No inkling/idea.
situation: Expressing complete lack of knowledge about a question.
culturalNote: One of the most frequently spoken colloquial phrases in daily German.

dialogue.speakerA: Weißt du, wann der Bus kommt?
dialogue.speakerB: Keine Ahnung, schau mal in die App.
dialogue.englishA: Do you know when the bus arrives?
dialogue.englishB: No idea, check the app.

german: Ich habe keinen blassen Schimmer!
english: I don't have the faintest clue / slightest idea!
literalTranslation: I have no pale shimmer!
situation: Emphatically stating total ignorance about a topic.
culturalNote: 'Schimmer' denotes a faint ray of light in the dark; having not even a pale ray means complete darkness/ignorance.

dialogue.speakerA: Wer hat das Passwort geändert?
dialogue.speakerB: Ich habe nicht den blassesten Schimmer!
dialogue.englishA: Who changed the password?
dialogue.englishB: I don't have the faintest clue!

german: Auf keinen Fall!
english: Under no circumstances! / No way! / Absolutely not!
literalTranslation: On no case!
situation: Firmly refusing or denying something.
culturalNote: Opposite of 'Auf jeden Fall' (Definitely / By all means).

dialogue.speakerA: Gehst du bei dem Sturm spazieren?
dialogue.speakerB: Auf keinen Fall! Da bleibe ich lieber drinnen.
dialogue.englishA: Are you going for a walk in this storm?
dialogue.englishB: No way! I'd rather stay inside.

german: Auf jeden Fall!
english: Definitely! / By all means! / In any case!
literalTranslation: On every case!
situation: Strong enthusiastic agreement.
culturalNote: One of the most common agreement phrases in German.

dialogue.speakerA: Kommst du heute Abend zur Party?
dialogue.speakerB: Auf jeden Fall, ich freue mich schon drauf!
dialogue.englishA: Are you coming to the party tonight?
dialogue.englishB: Definitely, I'm already looking forward to it!

german: Das macht überhaupt nichts.
english: That doesn't matter at all. / No worries at all.
literalTranslation: That makes at-all nothing.
situation: Graciously accepting an apology for an accidental mishap.
culturalNote: Reassures the other person that no damage or offense was taken.

dialogue.speakerA: Entschuldigung, ich habe versehentlich Kaffee verschüttet!
dialogue.speakerB: Das macht überhaupt nichts, ich hole kurz ein Tuch.
dialogue.englishA: Excuse me, I accidentally spilled coffee!
dialogue.englishB: That doesn't matter at all, I'll grab a cloth in a second.

german: Halb so wild!
english: Not a big deal! / Don't worry about it!
literalTranslation: Half as wild!
situation: Calming someone who is overreacting to a minor mistake or scrape.
culturalNote: Classic German phrase to de-escalate minor everyday troubles.

dialogue.speakerA: Es tut mir so leid, dass ich zu spät bin!
dialogue.speakerB: Halb so wild, wir haben gerade erst angefangen.
dialogue.englishA: I'm so sorry that I'm late!
dialogue.englishB: Not a big deal, we only just started.

german: Wie bitte?
english: Pardon? / Come again? / What did you say?
literalTranslation: How please?
situation: Politely asking someone to repeat what they just said because you didn't catch it.
culturalNote: Far more polite than saying 'Was?' (What?).

dialogue.speakerA: Könnten Sie bitte das Fenster schließen?
dialogue.speakerB: Wie bitte? Die Musik ist so laut.
dialogue.englishA: Could you please close the window?
dialogue.englishB: Pardon? The music is so loud.

german: Es kommt darauf an.
english: It depends.
literalTranslation: It comes thereon on.
situation: Expressing that an answer depends on specific conditions or factors.
culturalNote: Essential phrase in discussions, negotiations, and nuanced questions.

dialogue.speakerA: Fährst du morgen mit dem Fahrrad zur Arbeit?
dialogue.speakerB: Es kommt darauf an, wie das Wetter wird.
dialogue.englishA: Are you riding your bike to work tomorrow?
dialogue.englishB: It depends on what the weather will be like.

german: Könnte ich bitte die Speisekarte auf Englisch haben?
english: Could I please have the menu in English?
literalTranslation: Could I please the menu in English have?
situation: When dining and requesting an English menu.
culturalNote: Most tourist and metropolitan restaurants have English menus available upon request.

dialogue.speakerA: Guten Abend! Was darf es sein?
dialogue.speakerB: Guten Abend! Könnte ich bitte die Speisekarte auf Englisch haben?
dialogue.englishA: Good evening! What can I get for you?
dialogue.englishB: Good evening! Could I please have the menu in English?

german: Ich bin allergisch gegen Nüsse und Erdnüsse.
english: I am allergic to nuts and peanuts.
literalTranslation: I am allergic against nuts and peanuts.
situation: Informing the server of food allergies.
culturalNote: German food labeling regulations strictly monitor tree nuts (Schalenfrüchte).

dialogue.speakerA: Haben Sie Allergien?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, ich bin allergisch gegen Nüsse und Erdnüsse.
dialogue.englishA: Do you have allergies?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, I am allergic to nuts and peanuts.

german: Gibt es in diesem Gericht Schweinefleisch?
english: Is there pork in this dish?
literalTranslation: Gives it in this dish pork-meat?
situation: Asking for dietary or religious pork avoidance.
culturalNote: Pork is prominent in traditional German cuisine, so asking is common.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen etwas empfehlen?
dialogue.speakerB: Gibt es in diesem Gericht Schweinefleisch?
dialogue.englishA: Can I recommend something?
dialogue.englishB: Is there pork in this dish?

german: Ich hätte gerne ein alkoholfreies Bier, bitte.
english: I would like a non-alcoholic beer, please.
literalTranslation: I would have gladly an alcohol-free beer, please.
situation: Ordering non-alcoholic beer in a restaurant or pub.
culturalNote: Germany produces world-renowned non-alcoholic beers (alkoholfrei).

dialogue.speakerA: Was möchten Sie trinken?
dialogue.speakerB: Ich hätte gerne ein alkoholfreies Bier, bitte.
dialogue.englishA: What would you like to drink?
dialogue.englishB: I would like a non-alcoholic beer, please.

german: Können Sie die Soße bitte separat servieren?
english: Could you please serve the sauce separately?
literalTranslation: Can you the sauce please separate serve?
situation: Requesting salad dressing or gravy on the side.
culturalNote: German waitstaff are happy to accommodate side sauces.

dialogue.speakerA: Möchten Sie Soße zum Schnitzel?
dialogue.speakerB: Können Sie die Soße bitte separat servieren?
dialogue.englishA: Would you like sauce with the schnitzel?
dialogue.englishB: Could you please serve the sauce separately?

german: Ist dieser Platz am Fenster noch frei?
english: Is this seat by the window still free?
literalTranslation: Is this place at-the window still free?
situation: Asking to sit near the window.
culturalNote: Window seats (Fensterplatz) are the most popular in German cafés.

dialogue.speakerA: Suchen Sie einen Platz?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, ist dieser Platz am Fenster noch frei?
dialogue.englishA: Are you looking for a seat?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, is this seat by the window still free?

german: Bringen Sie uns bitte noch zwei Gläser.
english: Please bring us two more glasses.
literalTranslation: Bring to-us please still two glasses.
situation: Asking for extra drinking glasses.
culturalNote: Simple and direct table request.

dialogue.speakerA: Brauchen Sie noch etwas für den Tisch?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, bringen Sie uns bitte noch zwei Gläser.
dialogue.englishA: Do you need anything else for the table?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, please bring us two more glasses.

german: Das Essen ist leider kalt.
english: The food is unfortunately cold.
literalTranslation: The food is unfortunately cold.
situation: Politely sending back food that arrived cold.
culturalNote: State politely to the waiter and they will gladly reheat or replace it.

dialogue.speakerA: Ist alles in Ordnung bei Ihnen?
dialogue.speakerB: Entschuldigung, aber das Essen ist leider kalt.
dialogue.englishA: Is everything alright with you?
dialogue.englishB: Excuse me, but the food is unfortunately cold.

german: Ich habe das falsche Gericht bekommen.
english: I received the wrong dish.
literalTranslation: I have the wrong dish received.
situation: Notifying the waiter of an order mix-up.
culturalNote: Waiters will quickly correct the order.

dialogue.speakerA: Guten Appetit!
dialogue.speakerB: Entschuldigung, ich glaube, ich habe das falsche Gericht bekommen.
dialogue.englishA: Enjoy your meal!
dialogue.englishB: Excuse me, I believe I received the wrong dish.

german: Wir warten schon seit einer halben Stunde.
english: We have been waiting for half an hour already.
literalTranslation: We wait already since a half hour.
situation: Inquiring politely about long waiting times.
culturalNote: Kitchen delays happen during peak weekend hours.

dialogue.speakerA: Entschuldigung, wir warten schon seit einer halben Stunde auf unser Essen.
dialogue.speakerB: Oh, Verzeihung! Ich frage sofort in der Küche nach.
dialogue.englishA: Excuse me, we have been waiting for half an hour for our food.
dialogue.englishB: Oh, pardon! I'll ask in the kitchen right away.

german: Lass uns bald mal wieder einen Kaffee trinken gehen!
english: Let's go grab a coffee again soon!
literalTranslation: Let us soon once again a coffee to-drink to-go!
situation: Friendly invitation to catch up with someone.
culturalNote: Classic informal way to maintain friendships in Germany.

dialogue.speakerA: Es war echt schön, dich zu treffen!
dialogue.speakerB: Ja! Lass uns bald mal wieder einen Kaffee trinken gehen!
dialogue.englishA: It was really nice meeting you!
dialogue.englishB: Yes! Let's go grab a coffee again soon!

german: Wie war dein Tag heute?
english: How was your day today?
literalTranslation: How was your day today?
situation: Asking a partner or roommate about their day.
culturalNote: Standard evening greeting at home.

dialogue.speakerA: Hallo Schatz! Wie war dein Tag heute?
dialogue.speakerB: Ganz gut, aber ziemlich anstrengend.
dialogue.englishA: Hello dear! How was your day today?
dialogue.englishB: Pretty good, but quite exhausting.

german: Ich bin heute total müde.
english: I am totally tired today.
literalTranslation: I am today totally tired.
situation: Expressing exhaustion or low energy.
culturalNote: Common empathetic conversation topic.

dialogue.speakerA: Kommst du noch mit ins Kino?
dialogue.speakerB: Nein danke, ich bin heute total müde.
dialogue.englishA: Are you still coming along to the cinema?
dialogue.englishB: No thanks, I'm totally tired today.

german: Was hast du Schönes am Wochenende gemacht?
english: What nice things did you do on the weekend?
literalTranslation: What have you of-nice on-the weekend done?
situation: Monday morning watercooler question at work.
culturalNote: Standard German Monday routine conversation.

dialogue.speakerA: Guten Morgen! Was hast du Schönes am Wochenende gemacht?
