dialogue.speakerB: Ich war im Schwarzwald wandern, das war herrlich!
dialogue.englishA: Good morning! What nice things did you do over the weekend?
dialogue.englishB: I went hiking in the Black Forest, it was glorious!

german: Ich freue mich schon riesig darauf!
english: I'm already looking forward to it hugely!
literalTranslation: I enjoy myself already hugely thereon-to!
situation: Expressing immense anticipation for an upcoming event or trip.
culturalNote: 'Sich auf etwas freuen' expresses future anticipation.

dialogue.speakerA: Kommst du morgen zum Konzert?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, ich freue mich schon riesig darauf!
dialogue.englishA: Are you coming to the concert tomorrow?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, I'm already looking forward to it immensely!

german: Hast du heute Abend schon etwas vor?
english: Do you have plans for tonight already?
literalTranslation: Have you today evening already something in-front?
situation: Asking someone out or inviting them to an evening event.
culturalNote: 'Etwas vorhaben' = to have plans.

dialogue.speakerA: Hast du heute Abend schon etwas vor?
dialogue.speakerB: Noch nichts Bestimmtes, warum fragst du?
dialogue.englishA: Do you have plans for tonight?
dialogue.englishB: Nothing specific yet, why do you ask?

german: Lange Rede, kurzer Sinn.
english: Long story short.
literalTranslation: Long speech, short sense.
situation: Summarizing a long story briskly.
culturalNote: Direct German equivalent of 'Long story short'.

dialogue.speakerA: Und was ist dann passiert?
dialogue.speakerB: Lange Rede, kurzer Sinn: Wir haben den Flug verpasst.
dialogue.englishA: And what happened then?
dialogue.englishB: Long story short: We missed the flight.

german: Da hast du vollkommen recht.
english: You are completely right about that.
literalTranslation: There have you completely right.
situation: Agreeing strongly with someone's point.
culturalNote: Polite and affirmative alignment.

dialogue.speakerA: Wir sollten früher losfahren, um Stau zu vermeiden.
dialogue.speakerB: Da hast du vollkommen recht!
dialogue.englishA: We should leave earlier to avoid traffic.
dialogue.englishB: You are completely right about that!

german: Ich bin ganz deiner Meinung.
english: I am completely of your opinion. / I agree entirely.
literalTranslation: I am completely of-your opinion.
situation: Formal/informal expression of complete agreement.
culturalNote: Used in debates and discussions.

dialogue.speakerA: Homeoffice spart so viel Pendelzeit.
dialogue.speakerB: Ich bin ganz deiner Meinung!
dialogue.englishA: Working from home saves so much commute time.
dialogue.englishB: I am completely of your opinion!

german: Wo finde ich die Milchprodukte?
english: Where do I find the dairy products?
literalTranslation: Where find I the milk-products?
situation: Asking a supermarket worker for product aisles.
culturalNote: Supermarkets in Germany group dairy under 'Molkereiprodukte'.

dialogue.speakerA: Entschuldigung, wo finde ich die Milchprodukte?
dialogue.speakerB: Gleich im Gang 3 auf der rechten Seite.
dialogue.englishA: Excuse me, where do I find the dairy products?
dialogue.englishB: Right in aisle 3 on the right hand side.

german: Haben Sie frisches Vollkornbrot?
english: Do you have fresh whole-grain bread?
literalTranslation: Have you fresh whole-grain-bread?
situation: Asking at a bakery for whole wheat/grain bread.
culturalNote: Germany is famous for over 3,000 varieties of sourdough and whole-grain breads.

dialogue.speakerA: Guten Tag! Haben Sie frisches Vollkornbrot?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, ganz frisch aus dem Ofen!
dialogue.englishA: Good day! Do you have fresh whole grain bread?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, fresh out of the oven!

german: Kann ich bitte eine Quittung haben?
english: Could I please have a written receipt?
literalTranslation: Can I please a receipt have?
situation: Requesting a detailed VAT invoice or receipt for business expense.
culturalNote: Required for business expense reimbursements (Bewirtungsbeleg).

dialogue.speakerA: Hier ist Ihr Wechselgeld.
dialogue.speakerB: Vielen Dank. Kann ich bitte eine Quittung haben?
dialogue.englishA: Here is your change.
dialogue.englishB: Thank you very much. Could I please have a receipt?

german: Gibt es darauf Garantie?
english: Is there a warranty on this?
literalTranslation: Gives it thereon guarantee?
situation: Inquiring about electronics warranty.
culturalNote: Standard EU statutory warranty is 2 years.

dialogue.speakerA: Ich interessiere mich für diese Kaffeemaschine. Gibt es darauf Garantie?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, zwei Jahre Herstellergarantie.
dialogue.englishA: I'm interested in this coffee maker. Is there a warranty on it?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, two years manufacturer warranty.

german: Ich hätte gerne 200 Gramm Gouda-Käse.
english: I would like 200 grams of Gouda cheese.
literalTranslation: I would have gladly 200 grams Gouda-cheese.
situation: Ordering sliced cheese at the deli counter.
culturalNote: Food counters in Germany measure deli meats and cheeses in grams.

dialogue.speakerA: Was darf es an der Frischetheke sein?
dialogue.speakerB: Ich hätte gerne 200 Gramm Gouda-Käse, bitte in Scheiben.
dialogue.englishA: What can I get you at the fresh counter?
dialogue.englishB: I would like 200 grams of Gouda cheese, sliced please.

german: Haben Sie das auch in Schwarz?
english: Do you have this in black too?
literalTranslation: Have you that also in black?
situation: Asking for color variants of shoes or clothes.
culturalNote: Helpful for retail shopping.

dialogue.speakerA: Die Tasche ist schön. Haben Sie das auch in Schwarz?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, ich hole sie Ihnen aus dem Lager.
dialogue.englishA: The bag is nice. Do you have this in black too?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, I'll fetch it for you from the stockroom.

german: Das ist mir leider etwas zu teuer.
english: That is unfortunately a bit too expensive for me.
literalTranslation: That is to-me unfortunately somewhat too expensive.
situation: Politely declining an item due to price.
culturalNote: Honest and standard shopping phrase.

dialogue.speakerA: Wie gefällt Ihnen diese Lederjacke?
dialogue.speakerB: Sie ist toll, aber das ist mir leider etwas zu teuer.
dialogue.englishA: How do you like this leather jacket?
dialogue.englishB: It's great, but that is unfortunately a bit too expensive for me.

german: Wo ist die Gepäckaufbewahrung?
english: Where is the luggage storage / left luggage?
literalTranslation: Where is the luggage-storage?
situation: Finding coin-operated lockers (Schließfächer) at a train station.
culturalNote: German train stations have automated locker cubicles for day bags.

dialogue.speakerA: Entschuldigung, wo ist die Gepäckaufbewahrung?
dialogue.speakerB: Im Untergeschoss neben Gleis 1.
dialogue.englishA: Excuse me, where is the luggage storage?
dialogue.englishB: In the basement next to track 1.

german: Kann man hier ein Fahrrad mieten?
english: Can one rent a bicycle here?
literalTranslation: Can one here a bicycle rent?
situation: Asking about bike rentals in German cities.
culturalNote: Cycling infrastructure (Radwege) is extensive across Germany.

dialogue.speakerA: Guten Tag, kann man hier Fahrräder mieten?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, für 12 Euro pro Tag inklusive Schloss.
dialogue.englishA: Good day, can one rent bicycles here?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, for 12 euros per day including lock.

german: Ist dieser Sitzplatz reserviert?
english: Is this seat reserved?
literalTranslation: Is this seat-place reserved?
situation: Checking digital reservation displays on ICE trains.
culturalNote: Small electronic displays above train seats show the reserved journey segment.

dialogue.speakerA: Entschuldigung, ist dieser Sitzplatz reserviert?
dialogue.speakerB: Nein, auf dem Display steht nichts. Sie können sich setzen.
dialogue.englishA: Excuse me, is this seat reserved?
dialogue.englishB: No, nothing is on the display. You can sit.

german: Wie viele Stationen sind es noch bis zum Marienplatz?
english: How many stops is it still to Marienplatz?
literalTranslation: How many stations are it still until to-the Marienplatz?
situation: Asking fellow passengers on the subway (U-Bahn).
culturalNote: Helpful when station announcements are hard to hear.

dialogue.speakerA: Entschuldigung, wie viele Stationen sind es noch bis zum Marienplatz?
dialogue.speakerB: Noch drei Stationen, Sie können sitzen bleiben.
dialogue.englishA: Excuse me, how many stops is it to Marienplatz?
dialogue.englishB: Three more stops, you can remain seated.

german: Der Bus fällt heute leider aus.
english: The bus is cancelled today, unfortunately.
literalTranslation: The bus falls today unfortunately out.
situation: Hearing about public transit cancellations.
culturalNote: 'Ausfallen' means to be cancelled.

dialogue.speakerA: Kommt die Linie 100 noch?
dialogue.speakerB: Nein, auf der Anzeigetafel steht: Der Bus fällt heute aus.
dialogue.englishA: Is bus line 100 still coming?
dialogue.englishB: No, the display says: The bus is cancelled today.

german: Ich bin momentan in einem Meeting.
english: I am currently in a meeting.
literalTranslation: I am currently in a meeting.
situation: Informing someone you are occupied.
culturalNote: Standard status update in workplace messengers (Slack/Teams).

dialogue.speakerA: Hast du kurz Zeit zum Telefonieren?
dialogue.speakerB: Nein, ich bin momentan in einem Meeting. Ich rufe dich später an.
dialogue.englishA: Do you have a moment to talk on the phone?
dialogue.englishB: No, I am currently in a meeting. I'll call you later.

german: Schicken Sie mir die Unterlagen bitte per E-Mail.
english: Please send me the documents via email.
literalTranslation: Send to-me the documents please per email.
situation: Requesting reports or PDF contracts.
culturalNote: Standard business request.

dialogue.speakerA: Ich habe den Vertrag fertig.
dialogue.speakerB: Super, schicken Sie mir die Unterlagen bitte per E-Mail.
dialogue.englishA: I have the contract ready.
dialogue.englishB: Great, please send me the documents via email.

german: Können wir den Termin um eine Stunde verschieben?
english: Could we postpone the appointment by one hour?
literalTranslation: Can we the appointment around one hour postpone?
situation: Rescheduling a meeting or appointment.
culturalNote: 'Termin verschieben' is standard calendar management.

dialogue.speakerA: Schaffst du es um 14 Uhr?
dialogue.speakerB: Es wird knapp. Können wir den Termin um eine Stunde verschieben?
dialogue.englishA: Will you make it at 2 PM?
dialogue.englishB: It will be tight. Could we postpone the appointment by one hour?

german: Ich wünsche Ihnen einen angenehmen Arbeitstag!
english: I wish you a pleasant workday!
literalTranslation: I wish to-you a pleasant work-day!
situation: Polite morning farewell to colleagues or business partners.
culturalNote: Formal and friendly workplace courtesy.

dialogue.speakerA: Ich gehe jetzt an meinen Platz.
dialogue.speakerB: Danke, ich wünsche Ihnen einen angenehmen Arbeitstag!
dialogue.englishA: I'm going to my desk now.
dialogue.englishB: Thank you, I wish you a pleasant workday!

german: Da steppt der Bär!
english: The party is really hopping! / It's wild there!
literalTranslation: There steps/dances the bear!
situation: Describing a lively, bustling party or festival.
culturalNote: From old fairground dancing bear shows.

dialogue.speakerA: Lohnt es sich, heute Abend in den Club zu gehen?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja absolut, da steppt heute der Bär!
dialogue.englishA: Is it worth going to the club tonight?
dialogue.englishB: Yes absolutely, it's really hopping there tonight!

german: Ich fall aus allen Wolken!
english: I'm completely flabbergasted / totally stunned!
literalTranslation: I fall out-of all clouds!
situation: Expressing shock at unexpected news.
culturalNote: Reflects falling from a state of bliss or ignorance to reality.

dialogue.speakerA: Hast du gehört, dass sie nach Australien auswandern?
dialogue.speakerB: Was?! Ich fall aus allen Wolken!
dialogue.englishA: Did you hear that they are emigrating to Australia?
dialogue.englishB: What?! I am completely flabbergasted!

german: Alles in Butter!
english: Everything is in order! / All fine and dandy!
literalTranslation: Everything in butter!
situation: Confirming that everything is safe and running smoothly.
culturalNote: Originates from transporting fragile Venetian glassware packed in cooled barrels of solidified butter to prevent breakage.

dialogue.speakerA: Gibt es Neuigkeiten zum Vertrag?
dialogue.speakerB: Alles in Butter, der Kunde hat unterschrieben!
dialogue.englishA: Any news regarding the contract?
dialogue.englishB: All fine and dandy, the client has signed!

german: Kalter Kaffee.
english: Old news / water under the bridge.
literalTranslation: Cold coffee.
situation: Dismissing something as outdated information.
culturalNote: Old news is as unappealing as cold leftover coffee.

dialogue.speakerA: Hast du gehört, dass der Chef kündigt?
dialogue.speakerB: Das ist doch schon kalter Kaffee, das weiß jeder!
dialogue.englishA: Did you hear that the boss is quitting?
dialogue.englishB: That's old news already, everybody knows that!

german: Herzlichen Glückwunsch zum Geburtstag!
english: Happy Birthday! / Heartfelt congratulations on your birthday!
literalTranslation: Heartfelt congratulation to-the birthday!
situation: The standard German birthday wish.
culturalNote: In Germany, wishing someone happy birthday before their actual birth date is considered bad luck.

dialogue.speakerA: Heute ist mein 30. Geburtstag!
dialogue.speakerB: Herzlichen Glückwunsch zum Geburtstag! Alles Gute für das neue Lebensjahr!
dialogue.englishA: Today is my 30th birthday!
dialogue.englishB: Happy Birthday! All the best for the new year of life!

german: Mein herzliches Beileid.
english: My sincere condolences / deepest sympathy.
literalTranslation: My heartfelt condolence.
situation: Offering sympathy upon learning of a bereavement.
culturalNote: Respectful expression of grief and support.

dialogue.speakerA: Mein Großvater ist gestern friedlich eingeschlafen.
dialogue.speakerB: Oh, mein herzliches Beileid. Ich wünsche dir und deiner Familie viel Kraft.
dialogue.englishA: My grandfather passed away peacefully yesterday.
dialogue.englishB: Oh, my sincere condolences. I wish you and your family much strength.

german: Ich bin stolz auf dich!
english: I am proud of you!
literalTranslation: I am proud onto you!
situation: Praising someone for an achievement or hard work.
culturalNote: Warm affirmation among friends, parents, and mentors.

dialogue.speakerA: Ich habe die Prüfung mit einer Eins bestanden!
dialogue.speakerB: Wahnsinn! Ich bin so stolz auf dich!
dialogue.englishA: I passed the exam with a top grade!
dialogue.englishB: Amazing! I am so proud of you!

german: Einen Cappuccino mit Hafermilch, bitte.
english: A cappuccino with oat milk, please.
literalTranslation: A cappuccino with oat-milk, please.
situation: Ordering coffee with plant milk in modern German cafés.
culturalNote: Plant-based milks like Hafermilch (oat milk) are widely available across German cities.

dialogue.speakerA: Was darf ich Ihnen bringen?
dialogue.speakerB: Einen Cappuccino mit Hafermilch, bitte.
dialogue.englishA: What can I get you?
dialogue.englishB: A cappuccino with oat milk, please.

german: Haben Sie laktosefreie Milch?
english: Do you have lactose-free milk?
literalTranslation: Have you lactose-free milk?
situation: Asking for lactose-free milk options in cafés.
culturalNote: Standard option in coffee houses.

dialogue.speakerA: Möchten Sie normale Milch?
dialogue.speakerB: Haben Sie vielleicht auch laktosefreie Milch?
dialogue.englishA: Would you like regular milk?
dialogue.englishB: Do you happen to have lactose-free milk as well?

german: Ein Stück Apfelkuchen zum Mitnehmen.
english: A piece of apple cake to go.
literalTranslation: A piece apple-cake to take-along.
situation: Ordering cake at a German bakery.
culturalNote: Kaffee und Kuchen (coffee and cake) is a classic 3-4 PM German afternoon ritual.

dialogue.speakerA: Darf es sonst noch etwas sein?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, bitte noch ein Stück Apfelkuchen zum Mitnehmen.
dialogue.englishA: Can it be anything else?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, please also a piece of apple cake to go.

german: Zwei Laugenstangen und ein Roggenbrot, bitte.
english: Two pretzel sticks and a rye bread, please.
literalTranslation: Two lye-sticks and a rye-bread, please.
situation: Ordering traditional German bakery bread.
culturalNote: Laugengebäck (pretzel dough pastries) is especially beloved in southern Germany.

dialogue.speakerA: Was darf es heute sein?
dialogue.speakerB: Zwei Laugenstangen und ein Roggenbrot, bitte.
dialogue.englishA: What can it be today?
dialogue.englishB: Two pretzel sticks and a rye bread, please.

german: Ist der Kuchen frisch gebacken?
english: Is the cake freshly baked?
literalTranslation: Is the cake fresh baked?
situation: Asking about bakery freshness.
culturalNote: German bakeries pride themselves on daily fresh baking (ofengefrischt).

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich den Pflaumenkuchen empfehlen?
dialogue.speakerB: Ist der Kuchen heute frisch gebacken?
dialogue.englishA: May I recommend the plum cake?
dialogue.englishB: Is the cake freshly baked today?

german: Haben Sie etwas gegen Kopfschmerzen?
english: Do you have something for headaches?
literalTranslation: Have you something against head-aches?
situation: Asking for pain relief at a German pharmacy.
culturalNote: In Germany, pain medication like Ibuprofen and Paracetamol is only sold inside pharmacies (Apotheken), not at supermarkets.

dialogue.speakerA: Guten Tag! Wie kann ich Ihnen helfen?
dialogue.speakerB: Guten Tag, haben Sie etwas gegen Kopfschmerzen?
dialogue.englishA: Good day! How can I help you?
dialogue.englishB: Good day, do you have something for headaches?

german: Ich brauche ein Rezept für dieses Medikament.
english: I need a prescription for this medication.
literalTranslation: I need a prescription for this medication.
situation: Inquiring if a medicine is prescription-only (rezeptpflichtig).
culturalNote: Stronger medications require a pink prescription slip (Rezept) from a German doctor.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich diese Tabletten so kaufen?
dialogue.speakerB: Nein, Sie brauchen ein Rezept für dieses Medikament.
dialogue.englishA: Can I buy these pills over the counter?
dialogue.englishB: No, you need a prescription for this medication.

german: Haben Sie Halstabletten gegen Halsschmerzen?
english: Do you have throat lozenges for a sore throat?
literalTranslation: Have you throat-tablets against throat-aches?
situation: Asking for throat relief.
culturalNote: Common request during winter months.

dialogue.speakerA: Was kann ich für Sie tun?
dialogue.speakerB: Haben Sie Halstabletten gegen Halsschmerzen?
dialogue.englishA: What can I do for you?
dialogue.englishB: Do you have throat lozenges for a sore throat?

german: Wie oft am Tag soll ich das einnehmen?
english: How many times a day should I take this?
literalTranslation: How often at-the day should I that in-take?
situation: Asking the pharmacist about dosage instructions.
culturalNote: Pharmacists write dosage instructions (e.g. '1-0-1') on medicine boxes.

dialogue.speakerA: Hier sind Ihre Tabletten.
dialogue.speakerB: Danke! Wie oft am Tag soll ich das einnehmen?
dialogue.englishA: Here are your pills.
dialogue.englishB: Thanks! How many times a day should I take this?

german: Haben Sie Pflaster und Verbandszeug?
english: Do you have band-aids and bandages?
literalTranslation: Have you plasters and bandage-stuff?
situation: Buying first aid supplies.
culturalNote: Essential vocabulary for minor injuries.

dialogue.speakerA: Brauchen Sie noch etwas?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, haben Sie auch Pflaster und Verbandszeug?
dialogue.englishA: Do you need anything else?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, do you also have band-aids and bandages?

german: Ich möchte gerne einchecken.
english: I would like to check in.
literalTranslation: I would like gladly to-in-check.
situation: Arriving at a hotel reception desk.
culturalNote: Standard hospitality greeting.

dialogue.speakerA: Guten Tag, willkommen im Hotel Stern!
dialogue.speakerB: Guten Tag, ich möchte gerne einchecken. Name ist Müller.
dialogue.englishA: Good day, welcome to Hotel Stern!
dialogue.englishB: Good day, I would like to check in. Name is Müller.

german: Wann gibt es morgens Frühstück?
english: When is breakfast served in the morning?
literalTranslation: When gives it in-the-morning breakfast?
situation: Inquiring about hotel breakfast buffet hours.
culturalNote: German hotel breakfasts (Frühstücksbuffet) typically run from 6:30 to 10:00 AM.

dialogue.speakerA: Hier ist Ihre Zimmerkarte.
dialogue.speakerB: Vielen Dank! Wann gibt es morgens Frühstück?
dialogue.englishA: Here is your room card.
dialogue.englishB: Thank you very much! When is breakfast served in the morning?

german: Gibt es hier kostenloses WLAN?
english: Is there free Wi-Fi here?
literalTranslation: Gives it here cost-free Wi-Fi?
situation: Asking for hotel or café Wi-Fi passwords.
culturalNote: WLAN is pronounced 'VAY-lahn' in German.

dialogue.speakerA: Brauchen Sie noch Informationen?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, wie lautet das Passwort für das kostenlose WLAN?
dialogue.englishA: Do you need any more information?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, what is the password for the free Wi-Fi?

german: Bis wann müssen wir auschecken?
english: By when do we have to check out?
literalTranslation: Until when must we out-check?
situation: Asking for departure check-out time.
culturalNote: Standard hotel checkout time is usually 11:00 AM.

dialogue.speakerA: Gibt es noch Fragen zum Aufenthalt?
dialogue.speakerB: Bis wann müssen wir morgen auschecken?
dialogue.englishA: Are there any more questions about your stay?
dialogue.englishB: By when do we have to check out tomorrow?

german: Könnten Sie mir ein Taxi rufen?
english: Could you call me a taxi?
literalTranslation: Could you to-me a taxi call?
situation: Asking hotel reception to order a cab.
culturalNote: Taxi dispatch services in Germany are reliable and prompt.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich sonst noch etwas für Sie tun?
dialogue.speakerB: Könnten Sie mir bitte ein Taxi zum Flughafen rufen?
dialogue.englishA: Can I do anything else for you?
dialogue.englishB: Could you please call me a taxi to the airport?

german: Können Sie mir bitte helfen?
english: Could you please help me?
literalTranslation: Can you to-me please help?
situation: Universal polite plea for assistance in public.
culturalNote: Direct, clear, and urgent without being impolite.

dialogue.speakerA: Entschuldigung, können Sie mir bitte helfen?
dialogue.speakerB: Natürlich! Was ist passiert?
dialogue.englishA: Excuse me, could you please help me?
dialogue.englishB: Of course! What happened?

german: Rufen Sie bitte einen Krankenwagen!
english: Please call an ambulance!
literalTranslation: Call you please a sick-wagon!
situation: Urgent request for emergency medical services (dial 112 in Germany).
culturalNote: Dialing 112 connects to fire and medical rescue anywhere in the European Union.

dialogue.speakerA: Hier ist jemand gestürzt!
dialogue.speakerB: Rufen Sie bitte sofort einen Krankenwagen!
dialogue.englishA: Someone fell over here!
dialogue.englishB: Please call an ambulance immediately!

german: Wo ist die nächste Polizeistation?
english: Where is the nearest police station?
literalTranslation: Where is the nearest police-station?
situation: Inquiring for police assistance (dial 110 for emergency police).
culturalNote: 110 is the nationwide emergency police dispatch number in Germany.

dialogue.speakerA: Ich habe meine Brieftasche verloren.
dialogue.speakerB: Die nächste Polizeistation ist gleich am Bahnhofsplatz.
dialogue.englishA: I lost my wallet.
dialogue.englishB: The nearest police station is right at station square.

german: Ich habe mich verlaufen.
english: I have gotten lost. / I lost my way.
literalTranslation: I have myself run-wrong.
situation: Admitting to being disoriented in an unfamiliar city.
culturalNote: 'Sich verlaufen' = lost on foot; 'Sich verfahren' = lost while driving.

dialogue.speakerA: Kann ich Ihnen den Weg zeigen?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja bitte, ich habe mich leider verlaufen.
dialogue.englishA: Can I show you the way?
dialogue.englishB: Yes please, I've gotten lost unfortunately.

german: Haben Sie mein Handy gesehen?
english: Have you seen my phone?
literalTranslation: Have you my mobile-phone seen?
situation: Asking if someone spotted a misplaced smartphone.
culturalNote: 'Handy' is the universal German word for cell phone.

dialogue.speakerA: Ich suche mein Handy. Haben Sie es hier gesehen?
dialogue.speakerB: Ja, es liegt dort drüben auf dem Tisch!
dialogue.englishA: I'm looking for my phone. Have you seen it here?
dialogue.englishB: Yes, it's lying over there on the table!

german: Vielen Dank für die Einladung zum Vorstellungsgespräch.
english: Thank you very much for the invitation to the job interview.
literalTranslation: Many thanks for the invitation to-the introduction-interview.
situation: Polite opening remark when meeting hiring managers.
culturalNote: Setting a professional, appreciative tone in German interviews.

dialogue.speakerA: Guten Tag, nehmen Sie bitte Platz.
dialogue.speakerB: Guten Tag! Vielen Dank für die Einladung zum Vorstellungsgespräch.
dialogue.englishA: Good day, please have a seat.
dialogue.englishB: Good day! Thank you very much for the invitation to the interview.

german: Was sind die nächsten Schritte im Bewerbungsprozess?
english: What are the next steps in the application process?
literalTranslation: What are the next steps in-the application-process?
